_why: Every candidate gate under tools/ and scripts/ that no check in scripts/ci-checks.mjs runs, with the reason it is not there. tools/gates/gate-registry.mjs fails when a candidate is in neither place, when an entry here outlives the file or the reason, and when a `red-on-main` entry points at a ledger heading docs/ideas.md does not carry. Written 2026-11-09 by Ursa's security seat, run 11, after registering the six that needed no excuse.
_kinds: See KINDS in tools/gates/gate-registry.mjs. A kind is not a severity: it says why no per-change gate runs this file, and each one is falsifiable by a different observation.

entries.why: It is the gate list. A list that ran itself as one of its own entries would recurse, and its own rules are asserted in scripts/ci-checks.test.mjs.
It reads `npm audit --json`, which resolves advisories against the public registry, so on a runner with no network it would report a clean floor over a scope it never measured.
Posting a message to the company board is an outward-facing write. A gate that posted on every push would put a seat's name on rows no seat wrote.
A PreToolUse hook that runs inside a seat's own session and decides one tool call. It has no verdict about a branch to fail on.
It asks what the board's checks actually prevented over a window of real traffic, through pageMessages in tools/board/page.mjs, so it needs BOARD_RUNTIME_TOKEN and answers nothing without it.
It counts what two board rules would do to the board's real traffic, which is a read of the live board rather than of this tree.
The board read this repository is allowed to use as the denominator of a ratio. It walks a cursor over the live message route and needs a credential a per-change gate is not given.
It decides whether each read filter filters by sending the route an impossible value, so its verdict is about the running board and not about the branch.
It grades every board route a charter names against the board that is actually running. Its `--gate` mode is a real gate and the thing it gates is the deployed board.

HQ's vendored L-X5 checker, which secret-print-tree runs through tools/secret-print-sweep.sh. The sweep and not the bare command, because three of the checker's five default scan roots do not exist here and a missing root is skipped in silence.
entries._note: Registering the bare command here instead of the sweep is the known hole; see the secret-print-tree comment in scripts/ci-checks.mjs.

entries.why: It reports every finding tools/instant.mjs's lint can produce and returns 0 on all of them. tools/instant-gate.mjs is the half that decides, and that is what instant-lint runs.

It asks the forge which rows are still open through `gh`, and it exits 2 when that read fails, on the stated ground that silence over a scope nothing measured reads as clean. Registering it with 2 tolerated would install exactly the defect its own header warns about.

The shared refusal three ledger gates call when they cannot establish their own premise. It owns the exit-3 code and the sentence, so it contains a process.exit and matches the candidate key, but it has no subject of its own to judge and no input to be pointed at. Its effect is asserted through the three gates that call it, in tools/ledger/ground.test.mjs and in each of their own suites.
It answers whether another open pull request already contains this one, which means reading the open set and fetching other branches' tips.

It classifies the collisions a merge queue cannot see across every open pull request, so it fetches every open head. Measured in this run: it had not finished after 40 seconds in a sandbox with the token set.
It names the register blocks two sides both wrote into, which is an instrument a seat reads while resolving a merge. Every outcome is information and none of them is a failure.

Its `--check` mode re-tests every urgent ledger entry against the repository, which includes `tools/secret-scan.mjs --history` over every blob in every ref. Measured in this run: still running at 90 seconds, on the same ground that keeps the history scan itself off a per-change gate.
It merges origin/main into every conflicting pull request's branch and pushes. A gate must never change the repository it is grading.
It measures whether GitHub's server-side merge honours a .gitattributes merge driver by creating the refs that would prove it, so running it is a write to the forge.
The git merge driver for docs/ideas.md, invoked by git during a merge through .gitattributes and tools/ledger/install-driver.sh. Its rules are asserted in its own suite, which tooling-suites runs.
The git merge driver for this repository's append-only registers, invoked by git during a merge through .gitattributes as `merge=register`.

The committed instrument behind every number in docs/design/register-merge.md, so a reader can re-derive them instead of trusting the document. It reproduces a past incident rather than judging the tree.

entries.why: A real gate and red: `--gate` exits 1 with 106 register read dates due. Every branch would inherit that red, and a gate whose light can only be cleared by work no branch contains is a gate every seat learns to ignore.

entries.why: A real gate and red: `--gate` exits 1 over 64 board notes its predecessor's time-keyed guard had called already answered. Same shape as read-dates above and the same repair.

It grades every tool path a standard or charter names against every root this host actually has, including other companies' checkouts under /srv/asc/repos. A GitHub runner has none of those roots, so it would answer differently about an unchanged tree.
It reads this run's own price out of the host's run logs under /srv/asc/state, which no runner grading a pull request has.
It asks whether the trunk is red and whether this seat did it, from a baseline recorded on one host at one commit. The question is about a run, not about the tree a gate is handed.
It says when a baseline and the repository it describes parted. Drift is a measurement a reader interprets, and the file reports it for every baseline rather than failing on any.
It asks how stale the charter each seat's run was actually handed, which needs the run feed and the forge rather than this tree.
The returning window's first instrument: how long this organization was dark, read off the live board and run feed.

It lists which open pull requests belong to a seat, through `gh`. Its `--audit` mode is a real gate over the anchored branch pattern and what it grades is the forge's pull request history, not the branch.
It asks whether anything licenses a reader to treat somebody else's draft pull request as abandoned, which is a question about live drafts.
It re-derives every number in draft-fault.mjs's measured block from the live repository, so it reads the forge for the same reason.

It merges every open pull request into a throwaway copy of main and runs the suites on the union. It fetches every open head and creates commits, so it is an experiment a seat runs rather than a verdict on one branch.

control: the trust layer between AI users and AI labs
entries.why: It asks whether a string on the base is actually unrepaired, which means reading the open pull requests that might already carry the repair.
For one open row it reports which files it rewrites, which it merely lags, and which it drags the trunk backwards. Three named outcomes a reviewer weighs, not a pass and a fail.
It reports the conflict surface of one pair of commits and requires `--head` or `--prs` to have a subject at all, so there is no tree-wide question for a gate to ask it.
It answers whether the text of an older branch is still in the tip, which is a question about two revisions a seat names rather than about the branch under test.
